prompt: The spec lists 'Out of scope: mobile app, other languages'.
tells: Out of scope: mobile app, other languages
trap: Nice-to-haves differ; these are explicitly out.

prompt: Every meeting added 'one small thing' until the two-week project took three months.
why: Work that keeps growing is scope creep. Draw the boundary.
trap: Prioritising helps, but the problem is no boundary.

prompt: Reports are moved to phase two so the first release can ship.
why: Deciding what's not in this release is setting scope.
trap: It ranks things, but the clue is drawing a line.

prompt: The team agrees to support only card payments at launch, not bank transfers.
why: Naming exactly what's included is scope.
trap: It's not an unusual case; it's a boundary.

prompt: New asks go to a list for later instead of into the current work.
tells: go to a list for later
why: Protecting the agreed scope from additions.
trap: It isn't asking why; it's holding the line.

prompt: The delivery app launches in one city first.
why: Limiting where it applies is scope.
trap: It names users, but by setting boundaries.
